question: What is the main job of the touch receptors found in the skin?

options.A: Holding the outer skin layer to the muscle below
options.B: Helping the body cool down by making sweat
options.C: Producing melanin to protect against the sun
options.D: Turning touch and temperature into electrical signals for the brain

explanation: Skin receptors specialize in converting physical feelings from the environment into nerve signals that travel to the brain. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is checking skin sensation especially important for patients who have had diabetes for a long time?

options.A: High blood sugar can damage peripheral nerves and reduce feeling
options.B: The outer skin layer gets too thick for receptors to work
options.C: Patients with diabetes sweat so much that skin receptors wash away
options.D: Blood flow improves so much that the skin becomes oversensitive

explanation: Long-term high blood sugar often leads to nerve damage, which lowers the ability to feel touch and temperature in the hands and feet. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h1)

question: How are encapsulated nerve endings different from free nerve endings?

options.A: They do not connect to the central nervous system at all
options.B: They are found only in the very top layer of the skin
options.C: They have a special connective tissue covering around them
options.D: They only carry chemical signals instead of electrical ones

explanation: Encapsulated receptors have a protective capsule of connective tissue that shapes how physical touch reaches the nerve fiber inside. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h2)

question: Where do touch and pain signals from the skin finally go so a person can feel them?

options.A: The somatosensory cortex in the brain
options.B: The sympathetic trunk along the spine
options.C: The motor cortex that controls movement
options.D: The front part of the spinal cord

explanation: Sensory signals travel up the spinal cord and brainstem to end in the somatosensory cortex, which lets a person consciously feel the sensation. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which skin receptor is mainly responsible for detecting fine details, shapes, and textures?
explanation: Merkel discs are slow-adapting receptors in the lower part of the epidermis that help sense edges, points, and textures clearly. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h3)

question: A patient holding a slippery glass feels it start to slide and quickly tightens their grip. Which receptors sensed that sudden slip?
explanation: Meissner corpuscles adapt quickly and are great at detecting low vibrations and objects slipping across the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h3)

question: What type of structures act as the main temperature sensors in the skin?
explanation: Temperature detection is handled by unencapsulated free nerve endings that respond to changes in heat and cold. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why does bath water feel less intensely hot after you have been sitting in it for a few minutes?

options.A: Blood vessels squeeze shut to block heat signals from the brain
options.B: Warm receptors destroy themselves when they first touch hot water
options.C: Temperature receptors adjust to constant heat over time
options.D: Skin cells quickly release cooling sweat to lower the temperature

explanation: Thermoreceptors fire fast when the temperature changes, but slow down if the temperature stays the same, causing the feeling to fade. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which nerve fibers send sharp, immediate pain signals quickly to the brain and spinal cord?
explanation: Myelinated A-delta fibers carry electrical signals fast, causing the first wave of sharp pain right after an injury. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h5)

question: Which of these does NOT activate pain receptors in the skin?

options.A: Extreme heat from an open flame
options.C: Gentle stroking with a soft cotton ball

explanation: Gentle touch stimulates light touch receptors like Meissner or Merkel corpuscles, not pain-sensing nociceptors. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why should a patient close their eyes during a routine skin sensation test?

options.A: To protect their eyes from bright room lights
options.B: To help them relax and lower their blood pressure
options.C: To activate brain centers for better memory
options.D: To stop them from using sight to guess where they are touched

explanation: Having the patient close their eyes ensures they rely only on skin feeling instead of watching the examiner's hand. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h6)

question: A student nurse is checking light touch on a patient's leg. What simple bedside tool works best for this test?

options.B: A glass tube filled with ice water

explanation: A wisp of cotton provides gentle contact that is ideal for testing superficial touch receptors without hurting the patient. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h6)
